name: System Hardening, Compliance & Secure Configuration
tagline: Audit, harden, and prove it: system security scans, compliance benchmarks, config automation, and network-service lockdown for defenders securing their own systems.

tools.name: Lynis
tools.desc: Agentless security-auditing tool for Linux, BSD, and macOS that runs 200+ checks across the whole OS, scores everything, and ends with a hardening index, disclosure status, and actionable remediation hints.
tools.when: First pass on any UNIX-like host you own — run a baseline audit, apply the suggestions, then re-run to watch the hardening index climb.

tools.name: OpenSCAP
tools.desc: NIST-certified SCAP 1.2 toolkit: loads security content (XCCDF/OVAL data streams) and evaluates or remediates a system against specific profiles from the command line.
tools.when: Repeatable, scriptable compliance evaluations against scap-security-guide content — the profile kills long manual audit checklists.

tools.name: auditd (Linux Audit)
tools.desc: Linux Audit framework userspace (auditd, auditctl, ausearch) recording privileged actions, file access, and security-relevant events to an immutable log across reboots.
tools.when: Build the audit trail that CIS/STIG rules require before the auditor arrives; verify live rules with auditctl -l and query with ausearch.

tools.name: CIS Ubuntu Linux Benchmark
tools.desc: Free CIS configuration guide for Ubuntu with scored and unscored hardening entries that scanners and auditors measure against.
tools.when: Hand-harden an Ubuntu/Debian-family host to a known-good baseline when no CIS-CAT scan is available.

tools.name: audit2allow
tools.desc: Core utility from policycoreutils that converts SELinux AVC denials from the audit log into targeted allow or dontaudit policy modules.
tools.when: See denials in journal/AVC logs and turn the desired ones into a proper local policy module instead of disabling SELinux.

tools.name: SETools
tools.desc: SELinux Project's policy analysis suite: seinfo, sesearch, sediff, sedta, seinfoflow, and the apol GUI for querying rules and information-flow in the installed policy.
tools.when: Reverse-engineer or audit what your SELinux policy actually allows between domains before writing new modules.

tools.name: SELinux Reference Policy
tools.desc: The community-maintained reference policy source tree that generated distributions extend; the base for understanding and building custom SELinux policy.
tools.when: Contribute to or build custom policy from source, or learn the module structure behind your distro's policy.

tools.name: ufw
tools.desc: Ubuntu's uncomplicated frontend over iptables: allow/deny rules for ports and services in a few commands, with sane IPv6 defaults and a status view.
tools.when: Simple proven host firewall on Debian/Ubuntu; default-deny inbound, allow only what a service genuinely needs.

tools.name: firewalld
tools.desc: Dynamic firewall daemon with zone-based policy, a D-Bus service API, and runtime-vs-permanent config separation; the default firewall manager on RHEL/CentOS/Fedora/SUSE.
tools.when: Host firewalling on RHEL-family systems: open only the services a zone needs and test in runtime before committing permanently.

tools.name: nftables
tools.desc: Netfilter's modern packet-filtering framework with a single, scriptable ruleset language that replaces iptables chains; the base engine ufw/firewalld sit on.
tools.when: Write a compact, atomic, version-controllable firewall ruleset for servers that need more control than ufw offers.

tools.name: ssh-audit
tools.desc: Audits SSH server and client configuration end-to-end: grades every KEX, cipher, MAC, and host-key algorithm, flags weak or vulnerable combos, and ships per-distro hardening guides.
tools.when: Audit sshd before changing anything, apply the printed hardening guide, then re-scan until all-secure.

tools.name: Mozilla OpenSSH Configuration
tools.desc: Reference hardening guide for sshd_config with Modern/Intermediate/MFA profiles and concrete HostKey, KEX, cipher, and MAC lists for each OpenSSH generation.
tools.when: Write a known-good SSH baseline, then confirm the result with ssh-audit.

tools.name: HardeningKitty
tools.desc: PowerShell tool that retrieves the current Windows configuration, assesses it against CIS Benchmarks, Microsoft baselines, STIG, and BSI guides, and can apply settings itself (HailMary mode).
tools.when: Automated CIS/Microsoft-baseline audit of Windows endpoints with minimal setup and a CSV scorecard.

tools.name: LGPO.exe
tools.desc: Microsoft's local group-policy utility (shipped in the Security Compliance Toolkit) that imports/repairs registry.pol files and audits local policy settings.
tools.when: Apply a downloaded security baseline GPO backup to standalone or non-domain machines and verify local policy compliance.
tools.install: Download from Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit (55319)

tools.name: CIS Microsoft Windows Benchmark
tools.desc: Free CIS configuration benchmark for Windows Server and client editions with scored and unscored hardening entries.
tools.when: Know exactly which GPO/registry settings an auditor will check, and harden by hand when scanner licensing is unavailable.

tools.name: Microsoft Security Baselines
tools.desc: Microsoft's recommended security configuration settings curated from the Windows Security Configuration Framework, shipped as GPO backups ready for LGPO import.
tools.when: Start from Microsoft's own baseline rather than writing group policy from scratch; the SCT download includes the LGPO import tooling.

tools.name: CIS Cisco IOS/XE Benchmark
tools.desc: CIS configuration benchmark covering Cisco IOS and IOS-XE: AAA, management-plane protection, SNMP, NTP, and platform-specific hardening entries.
tools.when: Hardening Cisco routers/switches to a defensible baseline before a compliance scan or external assessment.

tools.name: MikroTik RouterOS Security Guide
tools.desc: RouterOS documentation covering access hardening, service lockdown, firewall filter rules, brute-force protection, and secure defaults for MikroTik devices.
tools.when: Locking down MikroTik routers/switches you manage: follow the guide, restrict winbox/API, and add the recommended filter rules.

tools.name: Batfish
tools.desc: Network configuration analyzer that parses real device configs and answers questions about reachability, ACLs, and announced routes without touching the network.
tools.when: Validate that hardening changes (ACLs, filters, BGP policies) don't break intended reachability before pushing them.

tools.name: testssl.sh
tools.desc: Command-line TLS checker that tests every cipher, protocol, certificate, and vulnerability (Heartbleed, ROBOT, BEAST, and friends) against a live endpoint and grades the config.
tools.when: Audit the TLS posture of every service you expose before and after removing weak ciphers and protocols.

tools.name: sslscan
tools.desc: Lightweight TLS/SSL scanner that enumerates supported ciphers, protocols, and certificate details using OpenSSL, ideal for scripting into pipeline checks.
tools.when: Quick scriptable cipher/protocol inventory across many hosts when you only need raw output, not a full report.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.desc: Aqua's all-in-one scanner for OS packages, SBOMs, IaC misconfigs, and Kubernetes manifests/contexts; as a k8s subcommand it scans your cluster's deployed workload posture.
tools.when: Scan container images in CI and scan the live cluster (trivy k8s) for image and config findings in one tool.

tools.name: kube-linter
tools.desc: StackRox's Kubernetes YAML checker with 50+ built-in lint checks for security anti-patterns such as privileged containers, runAsRoot, and host-network exposure.
tools.when: Catch obvious YAML security anti-patterns in Git before charts reach the cluster.

tools.name: checkov
tools.desc: Bridgecrew/Prisma's policy-as-code scanner for Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfile, and more, with 1000+ built-in checks including CIS Kubernetes.
tools.when: Unified IaC-and-manifest scanning across your whole infrastructure-as-code estate in CI.

tools.name: kubesec
tools.desc: Risk analysis tool that scores Kubernetes resources on 10+ security criteria (privileges, capabilities, runAsNonRoot) and returns a risk score with pointers.
tools.when: Ten-second risk score for a single manifest before deploy or during review.

tools.name: kube-bench
tools.desc: Aqua's CIS Kubernetes Benchmark checker: audits control plane, etcd, worker nodes, and RBAC against the official benchmark, runnable as a DaemonSet or binary.
tools.when: Prove your cluster meets the CIS Kubernetes benchmark and track remediation over time.

tools.name: kubescape
tools.desc: ARMO's Kubernetes posture scanner covering NSA/CISA hardening guidance, MITRE ATT&CK, and 50+ frameworks, plus admission-controller enforcement of failed controls.
tools.when: Full-framework posture scanning of a live cluster that goes beyond the CIS benchmark into runtime control enforcement.

tools.name: Istio
tools.desc: Service mesh providing mTLS between workloads, authorization policies (peer/request authentication), and encrypted east-west traffic for zero-trust workload identity.
tools.when: Enforce workload-to-workload mTLS and least-privilege authorization policies in a cluster that already runs a mesh.

tools.name: Cilium
tools.desc: eBPF-based CNI that enforces identity-aware L3-L7 NetworkPolicies without sidecars, including encrypted traffic and observability at scale.
tools.when: Enforce zero-trust network policy at the CNI layer when you don't want to adopt a full sidecar-based mesh.

tools.name: CIS Cloud Benchmarks
tools.desc: Free CIS benchmark sets for AWS, Azure, and GCP covering IAM, storage, networking, logging, and monitoring controls in each provider's console-accessible language.
tools.when: Know which cloud console/service settings an auditor checks, provider by provider.

tools.name: Prowler
tools.desc: Runs 1,000+ read-only checks across AWS, Azure, and GCP against CIS Benchmarks and 70+ compliance frameworks, with remediation guidance per finding.
tools.when: Default CIS/NIST posture review of any account you own; the coverage map and remediation pointers make fixing straightforward.

tools.name: Scout Suite
tools.desc: NCC Group's multi-cloud auditor pulls configuration from provider APIs and renders a browsable point-in-time HTML report of risk areas for AWS, Azure, and GCP.
tools.when: A clean visual HTML report of config risk in one account as a second opinion alongside Prowler.

tools.name: scap-security-guide
tools.desc: OpenSCAP's official security content: prebuilt SCAP data streams with profiles for CIS, DISA STIG, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA, plus bundled bash and Ansible remediation scripts that apply the fixes.
tools.when: Every compliance scan starts here — grab the data stream for your distro, feed it to openscap, review failures, then remediate with the generated scripts.

tools.name: CIS Benchmarks
tools.desc: Free, consensus-built configuration guides (PDF) for hundreds of OS, server, cloud, and application targets — the de-facto hardening standard auditors and scanners measure against.
tools.when: Hand-hardening to a known-good baseline with no scanner available; open the benchmark PDF for your platform and apply the entries manually.
tools.install: preinstalled (web) — free PDF download after registering a CIS account

tools.name: STIG Viewer
tools.desc: Browser database of the entire DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide set — rule-by-rule requirements with severity, CCI/NIST 800-53 mappings, and concrete fix text.
tools.when: Federal or DISA-style compliance: look up the exact configuration a STIG rule demands before touching config files.

tools.name: InSpec
tools.desc: Chef's open-source compliance language that turns CIS/STIG baselines into executable profile code (many public profiles exist) and runs them over local and remote systems.
tools.when: Version-controllable, reusable compliance profiles that you run in CI or on-demand without a commercial scanner.

tools.name: CIS-CAT Pro Assessor
tools.desc: Commercial CIS scanner (SecureSuite membership) that turns CIS Benchmarks into automated scans and compliance score/report output; a free CIS-CAT Lite covers a small set of select benchmarks.
tools.when: Audits that must document conformance to a specific CIS Benchmark version with vendor-supported mapping and reporting.

tools.name: ansible-hardening
tools.desc: dev-sec's battle-tested Ansible collection (devsec.hardening) that hardens OS, SSH, nginx, and MySQL/MariaDB at scale, aligned with the InSpec baselines the same team maintains.
tools.when: Apply the same hardening repeatedly to many hosts you manage — idempotent automation beats hand-editing configs on every box.

tools.name: systemd-analyze security
tools.desc: Built-in systemd command that scores each service unit 0-10 on exposure (PrivateTmp, NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, and more) and lists the exact directives dragging the score down.
tools.when: Zero-install per-service hardening review on any systemd host — tighten the worst offenders on long-running units.
